name: Seated Pelvic Tilt & Rib Stack
cues: Sit on your sit-bones, feet flat
Gently roll the pelvis under, like tucking a tail
Exhale as you tuck — ribs drop over the pelvis
mistakes: Slumping the whole spine instead of tilting the pelvis
regression: Smaller range, hands on thighs for feedback

name: Seated Scapular Pinch & Set
cues: Sit tall, arms relaxed
Pinch the shoulder blades together and down, toward the back pockets
Neck stays long — chin lightly tucked
mistakes: Shrugging up instead of sliding down
Arching the low back to fake the pinch
progression: Add a chin tuck to every rep

name: Standing Wall Posture Reset
cues: Three points on the wall: tailbone, shoulder blades, head
Chin in — do not look up to force head contact
Breathe: if you cannot breathe, you are forcing it
mistakes: Arching the low back off the wall
regression: Head off the wall with chin tucked — measure the gap shrinking over weeks
progression: Add 10 wall angels from this position

name: Seated Thoracic Opener (chair back)
cues: Chair-back edge at the MID-back, never the low back
Hands cradle the head, elbows wide
Small range, exhale as you open. Stop if anything refers down the leg
mistakes: Edge at the low back — that is lumbar extension, banned here
regression: Rolled towel over the chair back, smaller range
progression: Move the edge one segment up per rep

name: Standing Glute Squeeze & Tilt
cues: Stand tall, feet hip-width, hand on a counter if needed
Squeeze the glutes and tip the belt buckle up toward the ribs
Ribs stay down — tall, not arched

name: Seated Desk Hip IR (no band)
cues: Sit tall at the chair edge, knee at 90°
Thigh pinned — swing the foot outward from the hip only
Slow: 2 seconds out, 2 back. Right side first + extra set
regression: Smaller range, hands gripping the chair seat
progression: Add the loop band version (seated hip IR)

name: Chair Sit-to-Stand
cues: Feet flat, hinge slightly from the hips
Drive through the heels to stand
Finish tall — glutes squeezed, pelvis tucked, do not arch
mistakes: Rounding then arching the low back
Pushing off with the hands (that is the regression, not the rep)

name: Standing Chest Opener (hands behind back)
cues: Clasp the hands behind your back
Straighten the arms gently and lift them a small way
Chest tall, chin tucked, ribs down — stretch in the chest, never the low back
regression: Hold a towel between the hands if the clasp does not reach
